result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.add_tadpole_graph()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a tadpole graph to the current graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5976-L6066){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.add_tadpole_graph( m, n, type=None, label=True, rel=None, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Tadpole graph](/assets/graphs/add-tadpole-graph.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three tadpole graphs side by side: a triangle with a one-node tail for m=3 and n=1, a square with a two-node tail, and a hexagon with a two-node tail. Unlike the lollipop, the head is a plain cycle, so every head node but the one holding the tail has two neighbors." width="100%"} Creates a cycle ("head") of `m` nodes with a path ("tail") of `n` more nodes hanging off one of them. The graph has `m + n` nodes and `m + n` edges, so it is connected with exactly one cycle (a unicyclic graph). With `n=0` it is just the cycle. Tadpoles are also called dragon or pan graphs (`n=1` gives the pan). The cycle is created first and the tail follows, attached to the cycle's last node. In a directed graph the cycle runs in one direction (each node to the next, the last back to the first) and the tail points away from the cycle. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Tadpole graphs are useful for: - test cases for cycle detection and girth, where the cycle sits off to one side - the sparse counterpart of the lollipop graph (see `add_lollipop_graph()`), for comparing measures on a ring with a tail - modeling a loop with a single access road (a circular route plus a spur line) ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [m]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in the cycle. Must be at least `3`. [n]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Number of nodes in the tail. Must be non-negative. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `m=` is less than `3` or `n=` is negative. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} A five-node cycle with a two-node tail has as many edges as nodes: ::: {#9040923a .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_tadpole_graph(m=5, n=2) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (7, 7) ``` ::: ::: The tail hangs from node `"5"`, which therefore has degree `3`, and the graph contains exactly one cycle, of length `m=5`: ::: {#ea2eaf81 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_degree("5"), graph.get_girth() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (3, 9) ``` ::: :::
